target.title: Doctor: audit lint default selection
target.body:
## Summary
- Rebases the lint-default audit after #100093 landed, so this PR now covers only the default-selection audit and docs/contract follow-up.
- Applies the lint-default changes chosen from the 48-check audit now that all 44 tracked Doctor rule families have structured lint findings.
- Moves historical/advisory or environment-inventory checks out of default `doctor --lint`: legacy state, session transcripts, session snapshots, and skills readiness now require `--all` or `--only`.
- Makes `defaultEnabled?: boolean` part of the public `HealthCheck` registration contract so core and plugin health checks can explicitly opt out of default lint while remaining selectable by `--all` / `--only`.
- Updates the Doctor docs to distinguish default `--lint`, full `--lint --all`, targeted `--only`, and `doctor --fix` repair policy.

## Default-lint contract
Default `doctor --lint` is the broad-safe automation profile: static/local, low-noise, and actionable for most users in CI or preflight output. Historical cleanup, optional inventory, live service state, account/channel-specific probes, and repair-oriented checks stay explicit via `doctor --lint --all` or `doctor --lint --only <id>`.

`doctor --fix` is intentionally not equivalent to `doctor --lint --all` plus writes. `--fix` does not accept `--all`; it runs Doctor's ordered repair path and only mutates areas with legacy repair logic or structured `repair()` implementations. Some lint findings are diagnostic only.

Finding level remains per finding (`info`, `warning`, or `error`), not per rule registration. The audit table includes the current expected severity range as review evidence, not as a public schema lock.

The full table below is review evidence from the audit. The code tests cover only the rules whose default behavior this PR changes; they do not freeze the full Doctor rule list as an executable schema.

target.title: fix(channels): normalize phone identities with stray plus signs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where phone-based channel identities could normalize to invalid values when input contained doubled or embedded `+` characters. In WhatsApp self-chat, allowlist, and phone-derived routing flows, equivalent phone numbers could fail to match if an operator copied a number with an extra plus sign or pasted a phone-like value with punctuation in the wrong place.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared `normalizeE164` helper now strips provider prefixes, keeps digits only, returns `+<digits>` for phone-like input, and returns an empty string when no digits remain. This preserves the existing loose E.164 contract while avoiding invalid `+...+...` identities across WhatsApp, Signal, iMessage, and other SDK callers.

This intentionally changes the exported Plugin SDK behavior for invalid/noisy phone input. The old `+` and embedded-plus outputs were not usable sender identities, and callers that already treat an empty normalized value as invalid now fail closed instead of comparing against a truthy non-phone identity.

The WhatsApp setup test mock was updated to mirror the shared helper so setup tests no longer preserve the old normalization bug.

## User Impact

Users who configure phone-based allowlists or self-chat behavior get more reliable matching when phone numbers include common copy/paste noise. A malformed-but-recoverable value like `++1234567890` or `1+234+567` now resolves to the same canonical identity as the clean number, so the bot is less likely to silently ignore an authorized sender or miss self-chat mode.

Invalid phone text no longer becomes the truthy identity `+`, which avoids storing or comparing against a value that cannot represent a real sender.

## Evidence

- Real after-fix helper proof:

  ```shell
  $ node --import tsx -e 'const { normalizeE164 } = await import("./src/utils.ts"); for (const input of ["++1234567890", "1+234+567", "not a phone number"]) console.log(`${JSON.stringify(input)} -> ${JSON.stringify(normalizeE164(input))}`);'
  "++1234567890" -> "+1234567890"
  "1+234+567" -> "+1234567"
  "not a phone number" -> ""
  ```

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/utils.test.ts` passed: 23/23 tests.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/channel.setup.test.ts` passed: 18/18 tests.
- `git diff --check` passed.

target.title: fix(ui): keep failed autonomous tool turns visible
target.body:
Closes #97849

## What Problem This Solves

When two autonomous agent turns are adjacent in Control UI history, a successful reply in the later turn could make a failed tool from the earlier turn render as `Tool output` instead of `Tool error`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway chat-history projection preserves `sessions_send` input provenance while displaying those messages as assistant-side forwarded groups. The Control UI now treats only groups with `kind: inter_session` and `sourceTool: sessions_send` as autonomous-turn boundaries before annotating tool outcomes.

The final implementation deliberately does not use `senderLabel` alone: ordinary relay-labeled assistant replies still count as replies to the current turn. It also preserves the existing behavior for non-text assistant content.

## User Impact

Earlier autonomous tool failures remain visibly failed when a later autonomous turn recovers, while normal labeled assistant replies continue to mark their own tool turn as successful.

## Evidence

Final head: `47a0e36593ddcf3532d88f158128e0f71c1af87d`

target.title: feat(channels): expose source actor attribution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Group-channel messages need a generic way to distinguish the runtime message author from the operator/user represented by the agent session. Without source actor attribution, downstream prompts, tools, and memory adapters can only see channel/session context and may conflate another group participant with the operator. This should be solved as a channel contract, not as a deployment-specific memory backend workaround.

## Summary

- Adds a generic `SourceActor` inbound context contract for the runtime identity of the message author.
- Maps Signal sender identity into `SourceActor` without making the contract Signal-specific.
- Types `SourceActorRole` as `operator | participant | self | system | external`.
- Documents `SourceActor` as canonical and the flattened `SourceActor*` fields as scalar mirrors for prompt templates.
- Exports `SourceActorContext` and `SourceActorRole` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime`.

## Stack

This is stacked after #96738 and `codex/signal-mention-facts-context`. Until those land, this PR's diff will include its dependencies.

## Production impact

No behavior change by itself. The change gives prompts, tools, and memory integrations a stable way to distinguish a group participant from the operator/user. Signal direct and group senders are represented as `participant` source actors.

## Evidence

- Channel context tests cover generic `SourceActor` projection and object-to-scalar mirror parity.
- Channel contract helpers now assert `SourceActor` scalar mirrors stay in sync with the canonical structured object.
- Signal mention-gating tests cover Signal sender identity mapping into the generic context.
- Plugin SDK runtime mock tests cover `SourceActor*` parity with production inbound context.
- Focused tests passed:
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/inbound-event/context.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/plugin-runtime-mock.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts`
- Plugin SDK API check passed without a baseline hash diff:
  `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check`
- Production TypeScript check passed:
  `pnpm tsgo:prod`

### Redacted Runtime Proof

Temporary local proof harness imported production `buildChannelInboundEventContext` and printed the emitted prompt context on PR head `5fab61f873`. The proof preserves the emitted source-actor shape while replacing all Signal identifiers, group identifiers, participant names, phone numbers, UUIDs, and message bodies with placeholders.

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module -e '<redacted proof harness>'
runtime-proof:environment
{
  "pr": 96863,
  "repo": "openclaw/openclaw",
  "head": "5fab61f873",
  "node": "v26.3.0"
}
runtime-proof:#96863 source actor fields emitted by prompt context
{
  "SourceActor": {
    "id": "signal:<redacted-phone>",
    "peerId": "signal:<redacted-uuid>",
    "displayName": "<redacted-display-name>",
    "role": "participant",
    "context": "signal-group:<redacted>"
  },
  "SourceActorId": "signal:<redacted-phone>",
  "SourceActorPeerId": "signal:<redacted-uuid>",
  "SourceActorDisplayName": "<redacted-display-name>",
  "SourceActorRole": "participant",
  "SourceActorContext": "signal-group:<redacted>",
  "scalarMirrorMatches": {
    "id": true,
    "peerId": true,
    "displayName": true,
    "role": true,
    "context": true
  }
}
```

### Operational Signal group evidence (2026-06-26)

A private Signal group smoke was run after a production config hotfix that kept the group-bound agent responding without changing Docker permissions. The private runtime intentionally stayed on its deployed OpenClaw release instead of being advanced to this PR stack today; the facts below are operational evidence for the real Signal group route, not an additional claim that this PR head is live-deployed.

Sanitized facts:

- `openclaw config validate` against `/run/user/1000/openclaw/openclaw.json`: `valid=true`, exit `0`.
- `openclaw-gateway.service`: `active/running`, `NRestarts=0`.

Deployment note: the private runtime is not being upgraded to this stack today because that would mix the PR validation with an unrelated Docker sandbox repair. The long-term Docker/rootless sandbox fix is being tracked separately.
## Tests

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/inbound-event/context.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/plugin-runtime-mock.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts`

target.title: feat(memory): carry source actor context into recall
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory recall can currently receive the conversation/session context without a stable indication of which group participant authored the triggering message. In multi-person channels, that can make retrieved or promoted memory read as if another participant's facts belong to the operator. This PR carries the generic source actor context into memory recall and prompt supplements so memory backends can preserve participant attribution without adding backend-specific logic.

## Summary

- Carries `SourceActor` from inbound context through embedded runs and plugin tool context.
- Exposes the same source actor context to memory corpus supplements for `memory_search` and `memory_get`.
- Reuses the typed `SourceActorRole` contract across reply runtime, plugin tool context, and memory context.
- Adds memory prompt/flush guidance to preserve participant attribution instead of merging another participant's facts into the operator/user profile.

## Scope and honesty

This PR carries `SourceActor` context into memory recall and adds prompt/flush guidance to preserve participant attribution. It is the plumbing + guidance layer: it makes attribution available and instructs the model to keep it. It does NOT yet structurally enforce attribution on stored memories (e.g., tagging persisted entries with the source actor) -- that is a follow-up. Best-effort: recall tracking never blocks recall.

## Stack

This is stacked after #96738, `codex/signal-mention-facts-context`, and `codex/source-actor-context-contract`. Until those land, this PR's diff will include its dependencies. Merge order should stay #96738 -> #96862 -> #96863 -> #96864, with later PRs rebased after earlier ones land.

## Diff shape

- Contract: source actor context and typed role reuse across reply/plugin/memory SDK types.
- Agent plumbing: inbound `SourceActor` is carried into embedded runs and plugin tool context.
- Memory core: `memory_search`/`memory_get` receive `sourceActor`; prompt/flush guidance mentions participant attribution.
- Signal prerequisite: mention context exposes delivered-turn mention facts only; skipped Signal turns do not create public prompt/tool context.
- Tests: channel/source actor parity, agent plugin context, auto-reply runner utils, memory-core source actor paths.
- Docs/API: channel plugin docs plus plugin SDK API baseline hash update.

## Production impact

No storage migration and no backend-specific behavior. This is not Honcho-specific: it adds a generic runtime/tool/memory contract that memory backends and supplements can consume. Core memory search still filters by existing session/source visibility; this PR does not claim a new per-person storage partition.

## Evidence

- Agent/tool context tests cover `SourceActor` propagation into plugin tool context.
- Auto-reply and inbound metadata tests cover carrying source actor context through reply runs.
- Memory-core tests cover source actor supplements in recall/citation paths and attribution guidance in memory output.

ClawSweeper now treats Mantis web UI chat proof as a supported proof lane in https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/424, but OpenClaw did not yet have a focused Mantis workflow that can run and publish that proof. This PR adds the OpenClaw side so `@openclaw-mantis web ui chat` has a real, bounded implementation instead of being only policy text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The intended scope is deliberately narrow: OpenClaw web UI chat transcript and chat interaction proof only. This does not make Mantis a general browser, WinUI, dashboard, settings-page, or arbitrary visual proof worker. Those surfaces should still use ordinary Playwright/browser proof, maintainer screenshots/manual proof, Crabbox where appropriate, or normal local artifacts.

target.title: fix(anthropic): keep OAuth callback on loopback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Anthropic OAuth allowed the local callback listener host to be configured without validating that it was loopback-only. The earlier PR revision also derived the OAuth `redirect_uri` from that bind host, but Anthropic's current client contract requires `http://localhost:53692/callback` even when the listener binds an equivalent loopback address.

Fixes #96485.

## Why This Change Was Made

The callback bind address and provider redirect identity are separate contracts:

- `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_CALLBACK_HOST` is validated only when login starts and accepts `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `::1`;
- the listener defaults to `127.0.0.1` and may bind any accepted loopback address;
- authorization URLs, manual-code prompts, and token exchange always use Anthropic's required `http://localhost:53692/callback`.

This is smaller and safer than deriving the redirect URI from local bind configuration. Direct inspection of the installed Claude Code 2.1.201 client confirmed the same contract: localhost redirect URI, loopback listener. Anthropic's public Claude Code issue #11469 documents the localhost callback behavior as well.

## User Impact

Invalid/non-loopback callback hosts fail only when Anthropic login starts, so unrelated CLI imports and commands remain unaffected. Operators can still choose IPv4 or IPv6 loopback binding without changing the provider-visible redirect URI.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwt6qx4r4ptdbg4ps3yhnj55`: `src/llm/utils/oauth/anthropic.test.ts`, 11/11 passed.
- The focused suite opens a real TCP callback listener on `127.0.0.1:53692`, sends an HTTP callback, and verifies both authorization and token-exchange requests use the fixed localhost redirect URI.
- Remote `oxfmt --check` passed for source and tests.
- Fresh full-diff autoreview: no actionable findings, confidence 0.96.
- `git diff --check` passed.

Live Anthropic token exchange was not run because it requires an interactive user credential. No docs change is needed; the Unreleased changelog entry is included.

target.title: fix(agents): send session_id affinity header to ChatGPT Responses backend
target.body:
Fixes #100232

### Problem
The agent-runtime OpenAI Responses transport (`createOpenAIResponsesClient` →
`buildOpenAIClientHeaders`) never sends a `session_id` header. The ChatGPT backend
(chatgpt.com/backend-api) routes requests by `session_id` — codex-cli sends it on every
request (thread id), and OpenClaw's own SSE/WS provider path (`openai-chatgpt-responses.ts`)
already sets it. Without it, each HTTP request from a session can land on a different
backend machine, whose local prompt cache doesn't hold the session's prefix.

Observed on live traffic (gpt-5.5, ChatGPT OAuth): cold-write streaks and *interleaved cache
lineages* — `cached_tokens` alternating between two values (e.g. ~28k and ~57k) across
consecutive turns of one session, i.e. two machines each holding a different partial prefix.
Aggregate TRUE cache hit rate ~47-56% vs codex-cli's ~92-96% on the same account/model.

### Fix
`buildOpenAIClientHeaders()` takes an optional `sessionId`; when
`usesNativeOpenAICodexResponsesBackend(model)` and no `session_id` was set by
caller/turn headers (caller-wins preserved), it adds `session_id: <sessionId>`. Threaded
from `options?.sessionId` at the single Responses-client call site. Scoped strictly to the
native ChatGPT/Codex backend — api.openai.com and proxy endpoints are untouched.

### Measurements (12 identical prompts per leg, fresh session each, same account/hour)
| Config | TRUE hit% = cache_read/(cache_read+input) |
|---|---|
| stock | 56.0% |
| + this fix (as a dist hot-patch) | **81.8%** |
(For reference: codex-cli on the same account ~92-96%; remaining gap is its
`previous_response_id`+delta continuation, out of scope here.)

A separate controlled A/B (identical tool-call sequences, same session shape) comparing
stock vs. the combined local fix set measured **45.9% → 92.0%** TRUE hit rate — 6.5x fewer
uncached input tokens for identical work (stock session `3017333e`: 466,088 uncached input
tokens; fixed session `b97d343e`: 71,478). This isolates the session_id header's own
contribution (56.0% → 81.8%, table above) from an additional byte-stable-prefix fix tracked
separately in a follow-up PR.

Also adds a NOTE comment (no behavior change) at the WS `websocketRequestId` fallback in
`openai-chatgpt-responses.ts`, which mints a fresh random id per request when
`options.sessionId` is absent — forfeiting affinity on that transport; worth a follow-up.

### Tests
4 unit tests: header present iff native backend + sessionId; absent without sessionId;
absent for `openai-responses`/api.openai.com; caller-supplied `session_id` not overwritten.
Typecheck (`run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json`) clean. (Vitest currently fails to launch
on this dev box for unrelated toolchain reasons — rolldown native binding; tests were
written against the existing patterns in `openai-transport-stream.test.ts`.)

Reported-by: @Peetiegonzalez
cc: @Peetiegonzalez

## What Problem This Solves

The ChatGPT Responses backend (chatgpt.com/backend-api) routes HTTP requests by `session_id`.
`buildOpenAIClientHeaders()` never sent one, so consecutive requests from the same OpenClaw
session could land on different backend machines, each holding a different partial prompt-cache
prefix — visible as interleaved cache lineages and cold-write streaks on live traffic. codex-cli
(external reference client) and OpenClaw's own WS/SSE path already send this header; only the
HTTP Responses transport used by the `openclaw` agent runtime was missing it. See "Problem" above
for the full mechanism and code path.

## Evidence

Measured, not estimated: 12 identical prompts per leg, fresh session each, same account and same
hour, ChatGPT-OAuth gpt-5.5, `TRUE hit% = cache_read / (cache_read + input)` computed from each
call's provider `usage` fields.

- Single-variable isolation (session_id header only, all else equal): **56.0% -> 81.8%** TRUE hit
  rate (+25.8 points), cache lineage streaks disappear.
- Combined with the companion byte-stability fix (#100272), same protocol: **45.9% -> 92.0%**
  TRUE hit rate, 6.5x fewer uncached input tokens for identical 12-turn work (466,088 -> 71,478
  uncached tokens).
- Full per-call tables, regression timeline (traced to a runtime-pin config change, not a code
  regression), and cross-provider blast-radius analysis:
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-session-affinity-header/pr-proof/100233-session-affinity-header/EVIDENCE.md

target.title: fix(agents): preserve media side merges during prompt release
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users sending multiple visible media replies while an embedded prompt lock is released could receive the media and then see the run fail with `session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released`.

This replaces #100033 with a current-main, maintainer-owned branch because the contributor fork could not be updated without retaining stale ancestry.

## Why This Change Was Made

Delivery mirrors append a side branch containing messages plus `leaf` controls. Prompt-release recovery previously classified the messages but treated every leaf control as an ownership takeover.

The new path accepts only side-mode leaf controls whose target remains the active leaf and whose append cursor matches the current side branch. Validation happens before mutation; active-branch changes, cursor resets, malformed records, and non-side controls still trigger takeover recovery.

## User Impact

Batched media replies can finish without a false post-delivery failure. The session ownership fence remains fail-closed for prompt-affecting changes.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox: 163 focused tests passed across `attempt.session-lock.test.ts` and `session-manager.test.ts`.

target.title: feat(ios): read-only offline cache for chat sessions and transcripts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where opening the chat tab showed a blank transcript until the gateway responded, and showed nothing at all when the gateway was unreachable. All chat state was in memory only, so cold opens and offline periods left users staring at an empty screen even for conversations they had just been reading.

Part of #100194

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a small, disposable, read-only offline cache of recent chat sessions and transcripts, scoped per paired gateway identity. Cold opens paint the last known transcript immediately; authoritative gateway history then replaces it through the existing reconciliation path. Post-send incomplete history cannot cache optimistic echoes or erase the last canonical snapshot.

The store is versioned SQLite with drop-and-rebuild on mismatch, bounded retention, no migrations, and no new dependency. Text rows only; attachment payloads and tool arguments are stripped. Each gateway gets a SHA-256-named database, so bootstrap replacement can retire and physically remove only that gateway's file and sidecars without deleting other paired gateways' caches. iOS opens cache files with Complete file protection and treats locked-device protected-data unavailability as a temporary cache miss.

## User Impact

The chat tab renders the last known conversation immediately on launch. Cached sessions remain visible and openable from Home, the full Sessions screen, and iPad Activity while disconnected. Sending stays disabled until the connection is healthy. Switching gateways rebuilds cache consumers immediately; reset/forget physically removes the appropriate cached conversation files.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto current `main`; final exact head: `b6ae8e17b97a4954129c223771e3bae51be6577b`.
- `swiftformat --lint --config config/swiftformat <17 touched Swift files>` — pass.
- `swiftlint lint --config apps/ios/.swiftlint.yml <touched Swift files>` — no new errors; only pre-existing size/complexity warnings.
- `node --import tsx scripts/native-app-i18n.ts check` — pass, 2542 entries, no drift.
- `node scripts/ios-write-swift-filelist.mjs` — pass; both new shared cache files are included in the iOS lint input.
- Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox `tbx_01kwt78aakecg7xbakwev6mxcn`: Linux Swift attempts reached existing Apple-only package blockers (`AudioToolbox`; then CoreFoundation symbols with Talk disabled) before these tests could run. The exact-head `macos-swift` and `ios-build` GitHub lanes are the compile/test gates.

target.title: fix #98107: Gateway regenerates service-env file on every restart, wiping Telegram bot tokens
target.body:
Closes #98107

## What Problem This Solves

macOS LaunchAgent regeneration could erase an active channel credential from the generated service-env file when the update/restart shell did not re-export that config SecretRef. The next gateway process then started without the token.

## Why This Change Was Made

The service install plan now receives the installed environment-value provenance and can retain an existing value only when all of these remain true:

- current config still references the normalized key as a SecretRef;
- the key is a safe service environment name;
- the installed value came from OpenClaw's generated file (`file` or `inline-and-file`).

The retained value is fallback-only: current state-dir dotenv, shell, and auth sources still win. Start-time stale-service repair forwards the same provenance into this one canonical plan.

Deep review found and fixed an important boundary bug in the earlier patch: filtering against all managed keys could resurrect a stale generated-file value after config moved the key to `env.vars`. The final code filters strictly against current config SecretRef keys. Retired refs, source migrations, unsafe keys, and inline-only values are dropped.

## User Impact

Gateway reinstall/update/restart no longer wipes active generated-file-backed SecretRef credentials merely because the invoking shell lacks them. Credential rotation and explicit current sources remain authoritative.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox: 49 focused tests passed (48 install-plan cases and one start-repair case).
- Regression coverage includes two active SecretRefs, retired managed keys, `env.vars` source migration, unsafe names, provenance filtering, and source precedence.
- Blacksmith Testbox: remote formatting passed for all touched files.

## Summary
- Rebases the lint-default audit after #100093 landed, so this PR now covers only the default-selection audit and docs/contract follow-up.
- Applies the lint-default changes chosen from the 48-check audit now that all 44 tracked Doctor rule families have structured lint findings.
- Moves historical/advisory or environment-inventory checks out of default `doctor --lint`: legacy state, session transcripts, session snapshots, and skills readiness now require `--all` or `--only`.
- Makes `defaultEnabled?: boolean` part of the public `HealthCheck` registration contract so core and plugin health checks can explicitly opt out of default lint while remaining selectable by `--all` / `--only`.
- Updates the Doctor docs to distinguish default `--lint`, full `--lint --all`, targeted `--only`, and `doctor --fix` repair policy.

## Default-lint contract
Default `doctor --lint` is the broad-safe automation profile: static/local, low-noise, and actionable for most users in CI or preflight output. ## What Problem This Solves

Group-channel messages need a generic way to distinguish the runtime message author from the operator/user represented by the agent session. Without source actor attribution, downstream prompts, tools, and memory adapters can only see channel/session context and may conflate another group participant with the operator. This should be solved as a channel contract, not as a deployment-specific memory backend workaround.

## Summary

- Adds a generic `SourceActor` inbound context contract for the runtime identity of the message author.
- Maps Signal sender identity into `SourceActor` without making the contract Signal-specific.
- Types `SourceActorRole` as `operator | participant | self | system | external`.
- Documents `SourceActor` as canonical and the flattened `SourceActor*` fields as scalar mirrors for prompt templates.
- Exports `SourceActorContext` and `SourceActorRole` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime`.

## Stack

This is stacked after #96738 and `codex/signal-mention-facts-context`. Until those land, this PR's diff will include its dependencies.

## Production impact

No behavior change by itself. The change gives prompts, tools, and memory integrations a stable way to distinguish a group participant from the operator/user. Signal direct and group senders are represented as `participant` source actors.

## Evidence

- Channel contract helpers now assert `SourceActor` scalar mirrors stay in sync with the canonical structured object.

target.title: fix(agents): bound body-less MCP HTTP text responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The MCP HTTP wrapper converted body-less foreign `Response` implementations by calling `text()`. That API materializes the complete remote body before OpenClaw can enforce a byte limit, so a hostile or compressed OAuth error response could exhaust memory.

Closes #97521.

## Why This Change Was Made

This takes the issue's fail-closed policy option. A body-less foreign response has no genuinely bounded reader: `Content-Length` is remote-controlled and can describe compressed wire bytes rather than decoded text. The wrapper now preserves status and headers but never calls `text()` or `arrayBuffer()` for that shape. Normal responses with readable body streams are unchanged.

The test rewrite removes repetitive response classes and covers missing, plausible, oversized, and dishonest `Content-Length` values. MCP SDK source was checked directly: `parseErrorResponse` reads the global `Response.text()`, so the synthesized empty body still produces a useful HTTP-status diagnostic without touching the foreign unbounded method.

## User Impact

Malformed/nonconforming body-less MCP OAuth responses now report a generic status-based OAuth error instead of preserving their raw error text. This is intentional: it removes the memory-exhaustion path while retaining status and headers. Standards-compliant streamed responses retain full error parsing.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwt6qx4r4ptdbg4ps3yhnj55`: `src/agents/mcp-http-fetch.test.ts`, 13/13 passed.
- Remote `oxfmt --check` passed for the changed source, tests, and changelog.
- Fresh full-diff autoreview after the fail-closed rewrite: no actionable findings, confidence 0.94.
- `git diff --check` passed.

No docs change is needed; the Unreleased changelog entry is included.

target.title: fix(skills): refuse owner-qualified ClawHub force install over a different owner
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Installing an owner-qualified ClawHub skill with `--force` over a skill already installed under a different owner silently destroys the existing skill and rewrites its tracking to the new owner. With `@alice/weather` installed, `openclaw skills install @bob/weather --force` reports success while replacing Alice's skill with Bob's under the same local name and flipping the lockfile and origin `ownerHandle` to `bob`. There is no way to keep both and no warning. The CLI itself recommends `--force` when a plain install errors with "already exists", so this is an easy path to data loss of installed state.

Introduced by the owner-qualified install support in #94282 (ebd87e7f37).

## Why This Change Was Made

The owner-mismatch invariant (an owner-qualified action must not act on a skill tracked under a different owner) is one rule shared by every ClawHub lifecycle entry point, but only the update and verify paths enforced it; the install path did not. `performClawHubSkillInstall` derives `targetDir` and the lock/origin key from the bare `params.slug` with the owner dropped into `ownerHandle`, and under `--force` the `pathExists(targetDir)` short-circuit is skipped and `installPackageDir` does a backup-then-replace, so an `@bob/weather` install lands directly on top of the tracked `@alice/weather`.

This change routes all three surfaces (install, update, verify) through one strict `assertClawHubOwnerMatch` helper instead of three near-identical inline checks. The helper refuses whenever a requested owner differs from the tracked owner, including a tracked skill that has no owner.

The install path differs from update and verify in one principled way: on install the requested owner is the actual download source, while on update and verify it is only a guard assertion (both always re-fetch from the tracked source). So the install path consults the guard only when the tracked skill already has a known owner; an owner-less (legacy) tracked skill falls through to the existing ClawHub release and trust checks instead of being reported as an owner mismatch. Update and verify keep their pre-existing strict behavior unchanged, including refusing an owner-qualified action against an owner-less tracked skill.

## User Impact

- `install @owner/skill --force` over a skill tracked under a different owner now fails with `Skill "<slug>" is tracked as @<tracked>/<slug>, not @<requested>/<slug>.` and leaves the installed skill, lockfile, and origin untouched.
- Fresh installs, same-owner force reinstalls, owner-less force installs, and same-owner updates are unaffected.
- No config, schema, or migration changes.
- The public skills CLI reference (`docs/cli/skills.md`) now documents the owner-qualified `--force` refusal and the preserved owner-less fallback, so the narrowed contract matches the shipped behavior.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/lifecycle/clawhub.test.ts`: 80 passed, including 5 new branch-complete regression cases (install different-owner refusal, install same-owner allowed, install owner-less fall-through, install owner-less with a blocked release, update owner-less refusal, verify owner-less refusal).
- oxlint on both changed files: clean.
- `docs/cli/skills.md` documents the narrowed `install --force` contract; `git diff --check` clean.
- tsgo not run locally (OOM-constrained host); CI covers the type pass.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: owner-qualified `install --force` over a skill tracked under a different owner must refuse instead of silently downloading over it and rewriting its owner tracking, while every sibling owner-guard branch keeps its existing behavior.
Real environment tested: the real exported lifecycle runtime functions installSkillFromClawHub, updateSkillsFromClawHub, and resolveClawHubSkillVerificationTarget, driven on a real on-disk workspace seeded with origin.json plus lock.json, with only the ClawHub network boundary stubbed at the infra seam; run on pristine main@87db23e543 and on PR head 4229215ce9 with identical inputs.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: a standalone driver (since deleted) calls each function for six owner-guard branches and writes the real result values (ok, error, resulting lock ownerHandle, whether the release was fetched, whether the package install ran) to a file, executed once on pristine main and once on the patched head.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 87db23e543)
S1 install @bob/weather --force over tracked @alice/weather: ok=true error=- lock=bob@1.0.0 resolutionFetched=true installRan=true
S2 install @alice/weather --force over tracked @alice/weather: ok=true lock=alice@1.0.0 installRan=true
S3 install @bob/weather --force over owner-less tracked weather: ok=true lock=bob@1.0.0 resolutionFetched=true installRan=true
S4 install @bob/weather --force over owner-less tracked weather, release blocked: ok=false error="Release weather@1.0.0 is blocked by ClawHub security review." installRan=false
S5 update @demo-owner/weather over owner-less tracked weather: rejected: Skill "weather" is tracked as weather, not @demo-owner/weather. resolutionFetched=false
S6 verify @other-owner/weather over owner-less tracked weather: ok=false error="Skill \"weather\" is tracked as weather, not @other-owner/weather."
# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs, head 4229215ce9)
S1 install @bob/weather --force over tracked @alice/weather: ok=false error="Skill \"weather\" is tracked as @alice/weather, not @bob/weather." lock=alice@1.0.0 resolutionFetched=false installRan=false
S2 install @alice/weather --force over tracked @alice/weather: ok=true lock=alice@1.0.0 installRan=true
S3 install @bob/weather --force over owner-less tracked weather: ok=true lock=bob@1.0.0 resolutionFetched=true installRan=true
S4 install @bob/weather --force over owner-less tracked weather, release blocked: ok=false error="Release weather@1.0.0 is blocked by ClawHub security review." installRan=false
S5 update @demo-owner/weather over owner-less tracked weather: rejected: Skill "weather" is tracked as weather, not @demo-owner/weather. resolutionFetched=false
S6 verify @other-owner/weather over owner-less tracked weather: ok=false error="Skill \"weather\" is tracked as weather, not @other-owner/weather."
```
Observed result after fix: only S1 moves, from a silent clobber on main (ok=true, lock owner flipped to bob, release fetched, package install ran) to a clean refusal on the patched head (ok=false with the tracked-owner error, lock owner stays alice, nothing fetched, nothing installed); S2 same-owner install, S3 owner-less fall-through, and S4 owner-less blocked release stay allowed or blocked exactly as before, and S5 update plus S6 verify keep refusing the owner-less mismatch, so the new guard fixes the clobber without over-firing or regressing any sibling branch.
What was not tested: no live ClawHub HTTP request (the registry boundary was stubbed at the infra seam); no full build or type pass on this host (OOM-constrained); the thin CLI wrapper around these functions was not separately re-driven.
Head note: the current head 646a1fed31 adds only the `docs/cli/skills.md` contract bullet on top of 4229215ce9; `src/skills/lifecycle/clawhub.ts` and `src/skills/lifecycle/clawhub.test.ts` are byte-identical between the two heads (`git diff 4229215ce9 646a1fed31 -- src/skills/lifecycle/` is empty), so the runtime before/after proof above carries forward unchanged. All 80 clawhub tests pass at 646a1fed31.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawSweeper now treats Mantis web UI chat proof as a supported proof lane in https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/424, but OpenClaw did not yet have a focused Mantis workflow that can run and publish that proof. This PR adds the OpenClaw side so `@openclaw-mantis web ui chat` has a real, bounded implementation instead of being only policy text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The intended scope is deliberately narrow: OpenClaw web UI chat transcript and chat interaction proof only. This does not make Mantis a general browser, WinUI, dashboard, settings-page, or arbitrary visual proof worker. Those surfaces should still use ordinary Playwright/browser proof, maintainer screenshots/manual proof, Crabbox where appropriate, or normal local artifacts.

## User Impact

Maintainers get a dedicated web UI chat proof lane that can validate a candidate ref, run a focused Control UI chat E2E proof, produce screenshot/video/metadata artifacts, and publish Mantis evidence for PR review. Contributors do not get a new product-facing UI feature.

## Implementation

- Adds `Mantis Web UI Chat Proof`, triggered by maintainer-authored PR comments or manual workflow dispatch.
- Validates candidate refs so the workflow only runs against main ancestry, release tags, or same-repo PR heads.
- Runs dependencies, Playwright browser install, and Vitest from the candidate checkout, while copying the trusted proof harness into the candidate worktree for stale candidates.
- Adds a focused Control UI chat proof that mocks Gateway traffic, sends a chat prompt, verifies the outgoing `chat.send`, renders a final assistant reply, and writes screenshot/video/metadata artifacts.
- Adds a trusted evidence manifest/report builder plus focused tests.
- Adds `web-ui-chat-proof` to the generic `Mantis Scenario` dispatcher and documents the lane scope in `docs/concepts/mantis.md`.
- Wires the new Mantis workflow into changed-file owner test routing and the package-acceptance artifact-upload contract regression test.

target.title: feat: add channel pairing request hook
target.body:
Related: #68214
Related: #89569

## What Problem This Solves

Operators can already approve pending DM pairing requests, but plugin authors do
not have a small, stable hook that fires when a new channel pairing request is
created. That makes common operator workflows harder than they should be:
notify the owner, write an audit record, open a ticket, or route the request to
an existing approval surface without polling pairing state.

Issue #68214 asked for an unauthorized/pre-auth hook surface, and review notes
there called the hook direction cleaner than adding one-off suppression config.
PR #89569 explores that broader access-request workflow, but it bundles the hook
with grouped allowlists, access-request behavior, trusted hook loading, command
changes, and channel-specific pre-auth message exposure. This PR keeps the first
step intentionally smaller: observe newly created pairing requests through the
shared pairing challenge path.

This does not close every ask in #68214: it does not expose allowlist-denial
events, add suppression semantics, or replace a future `message:unauthorized` /
access-denied hook. It is the narrower pairing-request notification primitive
that can land independently and coexist with a broader access-policy hook if
maintainers want that later.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a typed plugin hook, `channel_pairing_requested`, dispatched when a
channel DM pairing request is successfully created.

The hook is deliberately observation-only and narrow:

- no config/env surface
- no allowlist migration
- no auto-approval
- no custom denial/reply workflow
- no raw inbound message body, media, or transcript exposure

The event carries only the data a trusted plugin needs for notification/audit:
channel, optional account ID, channel-scoped sender ID, pairing code, and
sender-supplied channel metadata. Hook dispatch is fire-and-forget from the
pairing flow; failures remain fail-open, and the hook has a short default
timeout so slow notification plugins are bounded independently of the requester
reply. The code is a live, single-use approval credential and should only be
delivered to trusted operator sinks; metadata is untrusted display identity text.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can now build lightweight operator-notification workflows for new
DM pairing requests without polling the pairing store or patching individual
channels.

Because the event is emitted from the shared pairing challenge helper, channels
that already use the common pairing issuer get the hook through the central
path. Existing channel call sites now pass their resolved account IDs into that
shared issuer so multi-account notifications can identify the correct account.

This does not change default channel behavior for users without a plugin hook:
pairing requests are still created the same way, existing requests are not
re-emitted, and requester replies are still sent through the existing channel
flow.

## Evidence


target.title: fix(anthropic): normalize tuple tool schemas for Opus 4.8
target.body:
## Summary

Normalize Anthropic tool input schemas so draft-07 tuple arrays are emitted as JSON Schema draft 2020-12 `prefixItems` before the Anthropic Messages payload is built.

## Issue/Motivation

Fixes #98588.

Anthropic Opus 4.8 validates tool `input_schema` using JSON Schema draft 2020-12 semantics and rejects schemas that still use the draft-07 tuple form:

```json
{
  "type": "array",
  "items": [{ "type": "integer" }, { "type": "integer" }],
  "additionalItems": false
}
```

The existing Anthropic projection already serializes/quarantines unsupported tool schemas, but it was forwarding tuple-array `items` unchanged. That can make `tools.profile: "coding"` unusable with Opus 4.8 even though the same tool surface works with older Anthropic-compatible models.

## What Problem This Solves

This keeps OpenClaw's coding-profile/runtime tools available on Anthropic Opus 4.8 by converting tuple schemas to the draft 2020-12 representation Anthropic accepts:

- `items: [schemaA, schemaB]` -> `prefixItems: [schemaA, schemaB]`
- `additionalItems: false` -> `items: false`
- schema-valued `additionalItems` -> schema-valued `items`

The normalization is Anthropic-specific and runs after the existing JSON-safe projection, so other provider projections keep their current behavior.

## Changes

- Add an Anthropic JSON Schema normalization step in `projectAnthropicTools`.
- Recursively convert nested draft-07 tuple array schemas to draft 2020-12 `prefixItems`.
- Preserve the original tool descriptor object by normalizing the serialized projection copy.
- Add regression coverage for top-level and nested tuple schemas.

## Testing

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic-tool-projection.test.ts` — passed, 2 tests.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic-tool-projection.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.test.ts` — passed, 52 tests.

target.title: fix(mattermost): preserve text-block boundaries in draft preview (#87322)
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #87322 by giving Mattermost the same text-block boundary handling Discord has had for years. Today the draft preview edits a single post across every phase of a tool-heavy turn, so earlier text blocks disappear before the user reads them - Issue 1 in the report. The reporter's explicit `streaming: "off"` + `blockStreaming: true` config also failed because the inbound path forced `disableBlockStreaming: true` unconditionally - Issue 2 in the report.

This PR keeps the existing canonical `streaming.mode: "off" | "partial" | "block" | "progress"` contract on main (`src/config/types.base.ts:12`) - no schema change, no new config keys.

## Behavior change

`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.ts` - inbound dispatch path (`monitorMattermostProvider`):

- **Block-reply path now honored when preview is off.** Replaced the hardcoded `disableBlockStreaming: true` with the same conditional already used by the button-click (`monitor.ts:832`) and slash-command (`monitor.ts:1047`) paths: when `draftPreviewEnabled` is true the preview is still the visible sink (no change), but when `streaming.mode === "off"` the path now honors the operator's explicit `account.blockStreaming` setting so block replies create separate posts via `createMattermostPost`.
- **Preview rotates at text-block boundaries when `streaming.mode === "block"`.** New `createMattermostDraftPreviewBoundaryController` in `draft-stream.ts` holds a "did we just stream something?" gate. At `onAssistantMessageStart`, `onReasoningEnd`, and `onToolStart` the controller calls `draftStream.forceNewMessage()` (the primitive already on the stream - `draft-stream.ts:133`) if and only if a draft update was emitted since the last boundary. The next `draftStream.update(...)` then runs the `else` arm of `sendOrEditStreamMessage` (`draft-stream.ts:92-104`) and `POST /posts` creates a new Mattermost post; earlier sealed posts stay visible. The gate is the same shape Discord uses (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.draft-preview.ts:132-138`) - back-to-back boundaries without content never emit empty preview posts.
- **All other modes unchanged.** `streaming.mode === "partial"` (default) keeps the edit-in-place feel. `"progress"` keeps its single rolling progress post. `"off"` keeps its no-preview behavior.

`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/draft-stream.ts` - added `createMattermostDraftPreviewBoundaryController({ enabled, forceNewMessage })`. Local helper, no exposure through `api.ts`.

`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/draft-stream.test.ts` - added unit tests for the controller (enabled/disabled, content gate, back-to-back boundaries) and for `draftStream.forceNewMessage()` itself (next update creates a new `POST /posts` call).

`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts` - extended the existing `vi.mock("./draft-stream.js", …)` shim with a no-op `createMattermostDraftPreviewBoundaryController` stub so the suite keeps wiring through the mocked draft module.

## Compatibility and exported surface (maintainer sign-off requested)

Two intentional changes need explicit maintainer acceptance before merge:

- **Visible delivery-shape change.** For `streaming.mode: "block"` and for preview-off `blockStreaming: true`, a tool-heavy turn now produces multiple visible Mattermost posts (one per text/tool boundary) instead of one repeatedly-edited post. This is the fix for #87322 (earlier blocks were being overwritten), but it is a user-visible change for operators already running those configurations. Default `streaming.mode: "partial"` and `"progress"` are unchanged, and `"off"` keeps its no-preview behavior.
- **Exported draft-loop surface.** This adds an optional `takePending?(): string` member to the exported `DraftStreamLoop` type (`src/plugin-sdk/channel-outbound`). It is additive and optional, so existing plugin-SDK implementors are not broken, but it is a plugin-SDK-adjacent surface change that maintainers should accept.

I cannot accept these on the maintainers' behalf; flagging them here so the delivery-shape and exported-type changes are an explicit pre-merge decision.

## Diff size

```
 docs/channels/mattermost.md                        |   6 +-
 docs/concepts/progress-drafts.md                   |  16 +-
 docs/concepts/streaming.md                         |   5 +-
 .../mattermost/src/mattermost/draft-stream.test.ts | 271 ++++++++++++++++++++-
 .../mattermost/src/mattermost/draft-stream.ts      |  76 ++++++-
 .../monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts           | 111 ++++++++++-
 extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.ts    |  34 ++-
 src/channels/draft-stream-loop.ts                  |  10 +
 8 files changed, 502 insertions(+), 27 deletions(-)
```

## Boundary flush (addresses ClawSweeper P1 finding)

ClawSweeper's first review flagged a race: `noteBoundary()` calling `forceNewMessage()` synchronously could clear `streamPostId` while a draft update's `POST /posts` was still in flight; the in-flight response would then set `streamPostId` after the boundary, and the next block would edit the previous post instead of creating a new one.

`forceNewMessage` is now async and awaits `loop.flush()` before clearing `streamPostId` and resetting pending state. The controller's `noteBoundary` is async too; the inbound-dispatch callbacks (`onAssistantMessageStart`, `onReasoningEnd`, `onToolStart`) await it before resetting `lastPartialText`. A new `draft-stream.test.ts` regression case (`flushes a pending in-flight create before forcing a new post`) holds the first `POST /posts` response promise, fires the boundary while the create is still in flight, then asserts the second block lands as a separate `POST /posts` (not a `PUT /posts/{id}` edit of the first post). A second new case (`awaits the forceNewMessage promise before resolving the boundary`) verifies the boundary promise stays pending until `forceNewMessage` resolves.

## Pending-partial boundary seal (addresses ClawSweeper re-review P1 at `draft-stream.ts:167-168`)

ClawSweeper's latest re-review flagged a deeper boundary race. When a block's first `POST /posts` create is still in flight and a later cumulative `onPartialReply` leaves text pending for the same block, `forceNewMessage` bumped `postGeneration` and cleared `streamPostId` before awaiting the in-flight create. When the create then resolved, its `gen === postGeneration` guard failed because the generation had already advanced, so the returned post id was discarded. `sealedPostId` had already been captured as `undefined`, so the pending text went out as a second `POST /posts` instead of editing the just-created post. A slow server left the user with both a stale partial post and the sealed block post.

Fix (`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/draft-stream.ts`): `forceNewMessage` takes the pending seal text first (cancelling the throttle timer), then synchronously bumps `postGeneration` and clears the live `streamPostId` before awaiting the in-flight create. Each create now records its post id keyed by the generation it was issued under (`createdPostIdsByGeneration`), so after the await the boundary recovers the finished block's real post id from that record and edits it with the pending cumulative text instead of creating a duplicate. Clearing the cursor before the await (rather than after) is what also makes the detach synchronous; see the next section for why that ordering is load-bearing under fire-and-forget callbacks.

Regression test (`draft-stream.test.ts`, `seals a pending partial onto the in-flight created post instead of duplicating it`): queues a second cumulative partial while the first create is held in flight, then fires the boundary and asserts the request sequence is `POST /posts` then `PUT /posts/post-1` (one create, one in-place edit). The previous ordering produced `['/posts', '/posts']` (two creates, the duplicate ClawSweeper flagged); the fix produces `['/posts', '/posts/post-1']`. The generation-keyed record is what lets the seal still find the just-created post id even though the generation is bumped before the await.

Block-mode tool-progress test correction (`monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts`): the `keeps consecutive tool-progress updates on one post in block streaming` case now drives three `bash` progress events with distinct commands and `detailMode: "raw"`. Bare same-tool progress with hidden detail renders to an identical preview line, and the progress compositor correctly dedups identical text to a single update, so the prior version asserted three preview updates against one rendered line. With distinct rendered lines the case now exercises its real intent: three in-place updates on one post, no boundary for same-tool progress, and exactly one boundary when a new tool starts.

## Synchronous boundary detach (addresses ClawSweeper re-review P1 at `draft-stream.ts:165-168`)

ClawSweeper's last re-review made the load-bearing point that the embedded-agent subscriber does not await the boundary callback. `onPartialReply`/`onReasoningStream` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.ts:281,1193`) and `onAssistantMessageStart`/`onReasoningEnd` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.ts:144,573,687`) are all dispatched with `void`. So the boundary callback's async tail is not sequenced before the next partial. With the previous ordering, `forceNewMessage` awaited the in-flight op *before* clearing `streamPostId`, which meant the live post id stayed attached to the finished block across the await. A partial for the next block that arrived during that await - flushing immediately once the throttle window was open - would read the still-attached `streamPostId` and `PUT` its text onto the previous block's post, overwriting it. Whether the overwrite happened depended on microtask ordering between the boundary's clear and the partial's flush, which is exactly the kind of "incorrect under the real caller" the finding called out.

Fix: `forceNewMessage` now bumps the generation and clears `streamPostId` synchronously, before it awaits anything. The instant the boundary fires, the live cursor is detached, so any fire-and-forget partial that arrives next deterministically opens a fresh post regardless of microtask ordering. The seal onto the previous block's in-flight create is preserved via the generation-keyed record described above. This is the "detach synchronously" option from the review.

Real behavior proof (live HTTP, fire-and-forget interleave): a loopback Mattermost v4 server (`POST /api/v4/posts` artificially held 120ms) driving the production `createMattermostDraftStream` over real `fetch` round-trips. Block #1 creates `post-1`; the throttle window is allowed to elapse; the boundary is then fired fire-and-forget (`void forceNewMessage()`, not awaited, as the embedded subscriber does), and block #2's partial arrives next. The same script was run against the committed pre-fix source (`56186cfe25`) and the fix.

BEFORE (committed `56186cfe25`):

```
AGENT      -> text block #1 ('Looking into the logs now...')  [creates first post]
MM SERVER  <- POST /posts (held 120ms) -> post-1  message="Looking into the logs now..."
   stream.postId() after block #1 = "post-1"
   (300ms elapsed: throttle window open, so the next update flushes immediately)
AGENT      -> onToolStart [BOUNDARY] fired fire-and-forget (void), NOT awaited
   stream.postId() immediately after boundary call = "post-1"
AGENT      -> text block #2 ('Found the bad commit. Reverting now.') arrives before boundary settles
MM SERVER  <- PUT  /posts/post-1  message="Found the bad commit. Reverting now."
===== RESULT =====
POST /posts (creates): 1  | PUT /posts/{id} (edits): 1
block #1 post (post-1) final visible message = "Found the bad commit. Reverting now."
=> block #1 post was OVERWRITTEN by block #2 (data loss).
```

AFTER (fix):

```
AGENT      -> text block #1 ('Looking into the logs now...')  [creates first post]
MM SERVER  <- POST /posts (held 120ms) -> post-1  message="Looking into the logs now..."
   stream.postId() after block #1 = "post-1"
   (300ms elapsed: throttle window open, so the next update flushes immediately)
AGENT      -> onToolStart [BOUNDARY] fired fire-and-forget (void), NOT awaited
   stream.postId() immediately after boundary call = undefined
AGENT      -> text block #2 ('Found the bad commit. Reverting now.') arrives before boundary settles
MM SERVER  <- POST /posts (held 120ms) -> post-2  message="Found the bad commit. Reverting now."
===== RESULT =====
POST /posts (creates): 2  | PUT /posts/{id} (edits): 0
block #1 post (post-1) final visible message = "Looking into the logs now..."
=> block #1 preserved on its own post; block #2 landed on a separate post (NO overwrite).
```

The one observable that flips the outcome is `stream.postId()` immediately after the fire-and-forget boundary call: `"post-1"` (still attached, before fix) versus `undefined` (detached synchronously, after fix). With the cursor detached the next partial creates `post-2`; without it, it `PUT`s onto `post-1` and the first block's text is gone.

Regression test (`draft-stream.test.ts`, `opens a fresh post for a partial that arrives before a fire-and-forget boundary settles`): fires `forceNewMessage()` without awaiting it, asserts `postId()` is already `undefined`, then updates with the next block's text and asserts two `POST /posts` creates (`post-1`, `post-2`) rather than an edit of `post-1`. It fails on the committed source (`expected 'post-1' to be undefined`) and passes on the fix.

## Boundary gate clobber (addresses ClawSweeper re-review P1 at `draft-stream.ts:78`)

ClawSweeper's last re-review found the matching race one level up, in the gate. `createMattermostDraftPreviewBoundaryController.noteBoundary()` left `hasStreamedContent` true while it awaited `forceNewMessage()`, then reset it to false after the await. Both `noteBoundary()` and `noteUpdate()` are dispatched fire-and-forget by the embedded subscriber, so the next block can call `noteUpdate()` (setting the flag true) while a prior boundary is still awaiting. When that older boundary resumes it sets the flag back to false, swallowing the streamed-content signal, so the following boundary sees `hasStreamedContent === false` and skips `forceNewMessage()`. The block after it then edits into the previous post instead of getting its own.

Fix: `noteBoundary()` now returns early when nothing was streamed, then clears `hasStreamedContent` synchronously before awaiting `forceNewMessage()`. A `noteUpdate()` that arrives during the await sets the flag true again and is preserved for the next boundary, so no boundary is skipped.

Real behavior proof through the actual embedded callback path (current head): rather than calling the controller directly, this proof drives the production `subscribeEmbeddedAgentSession` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.ts`) and lets it dispatch `onAssistantMessageStart` and `onPartialReply` with its real `void` fire-and-forget semantics. Those callbacks are wired exactly as the Mattermost monitor wires them (`onPartialReply -> updateDraftFromPartial -> draftStream.update + noteUpdate`; `onAssistantMessageStart -> await noteBoundary`) against the production `createMattermostDraftStream` + `createMattermostDraftPreviewBoundaryController` over the loopback Mattermost v4 server. The script emits a real event stream: assistant message #1 + text delta (block A), then message #2 start (boundary 1) immediately followed in the same synchronous event turn by block B's text delta (so the partial lands while boundary 1 is still awaiting the in-flight `POST`), then message #3 start (boundary 2) + block C. Run against the committed head (`c8c90e0df8`, gate unfixed) and the fix.

BEFORE (committed `c8c90e0df8`, buggy gate):

```
AGENT(real embedded events) -> assistant message #1 (block A)
MM SERVER  <- POST /posts (held 120ms) -> post-1  message="Block A: looking into the logs"
AGENT -> assistant message #2 START [BOUNDARY 1] (subscriber dispatches onAssistantMessageStart with void)
AGENT -> block B text_delta arrives via the SAME synchronous event turn (onPartialReply void)
MM SERVER  <- POST /posts (held 120ms) -> post-2  message="Block B: found the bad commit"
AGENT -> assistant message #3 START [BOUNDARY 2]
MM SERVER  <- PUT  /posts/post-2  message="Block C: reverted, watching CI"
===== RESULT (driven entirely through subscribeEmbeddedAgentSession) =====
POST /posts (creates): 2  | PUT /posts/{id} (edits): 1
   post-1 final message="Block A: looking into the logs"
   post-2 final message="Block C: reverted, watching CI"
distinct posts: 2
=> only 2 posts: a boundary was skipped and a block was overwritten (data loss).
```

AFTER (fix):

```
AGENT(real embedded events) -> assistant message #1 (block A)
MM SERVER  <- POST /posts (held 120ms) -> post-1  message="Block A: looking into the logs"
AGENT -> assistant message #2 START [BOUNDARY 1] (subscriber dispatches onAssistantMessageStart with void)
AGENT -> block B text_delta arrives via the SAME synchronous event turn (onPartialReply void)
MM SERVER  <- POST /posts (held 120ms) -> post-2  message="Block B: found the bad commit"
AGENT -> assistant message #3 START [BOUNDARY 2]
MM SERVER  <- POST /posts (held 120ms) -> post-3  message="Block C: reverted, watching CI"
===== RESULT (driven entirely through subscribeEmbeddedAgentSession) =====
POST /posts (creates): 3  | PUT /posts/{id} (edits): 0
   post-1 final message="Block A: looking into the logs"
   post-2 final message="Block B: found the bad commit"
   post-3 final message="Block C: reverted, watching CI"
distinct posts: 3
=> all three blocks preserved on separate posts (real embedded callback ordering).
```

Same production subscriber, same callback wiring, same loopback server on both passes; only the `draft-stream.ts` source differs. Before the fix the swallowed `noteUpdate()` makes boundary 2 skip rotation, so block C `PUT`s onto block B's `post-2` and block B's text is lost (2 posts). After the fix boundary 2 rotates and block C lands on `post-3` (3 posts). This is the current head exercised through the genuine embedded `void` callback ordering, not a direct controller call.

Regression test (`draft-stream.test.ts`, `splits the next boundary when a noteUpdate arrives while the prior boundary is pending`): holds `forceNewMessage()` in flight for the first boundary, calls `noteUpdate()` during that await, releases, then fires a second boundary and asserts `forceNewMessage` is called twice. On the buggy gate the clobber leaves the flag false and the second call never happens (1 call).

Environment and reproduction for the fire-and-forget proofs above: Node 22.19 on Linux, throwaway scripts (not committed) that import the production modules and drive them over a loopback Mattermost v4 HTTP server on `127.0.0.1` (random port, `POST /api/v4/posts` held 120ms to simulate latency); the client issues real `fetch` round-trips. The gate-clobber proof additionally drives the production `subscribeEmbeddedAgentSession` and lets it dispatch the callbacks with its real `void` semantics (no direct controller calls). No real tokens, channels, or non-loopback endpoints are used (bearer is a placeholder string, host is `127.0.0.1`). Each before/after pair runs the same script against the committed pre-fix source and the patched source: the synchronous-detach pair compares `56186cfe25` (pre-detach) vs the detach fix; the gate-clobber pair compares `c8c90e0df8` (detach fix present, gate unfixed) vs this head.

## Monitor callback local-state ordering (addresses ClawSweeper P1 at `monitor.ts:1950`)

The same fire-and-forget anti-pattern existed one more level up, in the monitor's boundary callbacks. `onAssistantMessageStart` and `onReasoningEnd` awaited `previewBoundaryController.noteBoundary()` and only afterward reset the per-turn local state (`lastPartialText = ""`, `progressDraft.reset()`). Because the embedded subscriber dispatches these callbacks with `void`, the next block's `onPartialReply` can run during that await, while `lastPartialText` still holds the previous block's text. `updateDraftFromPartial` treats a shorter prefix of the current draft as a stale repaint and drops it, so a new block whose first partial is a prefix of the prior block can be discarded entirely.

Fix (`monitor.ts`): both callbacks now start the split, reset the local state synchronously, then await: `const boundarySettled = previewBoundaryController.noteBoundary(); lastPartialText = ""; progressDraft.reset(); ... await boundarySettled;`. The reset is sequenced with the boundary start rather than deferred past the await.

Real behavior proof through the embedded path (same `subscribeEmbeddedAgentSession` harness, current head, only the `onAssistantMessageStart` ordering toggled to mirror the monitor before/after): block A streams a long line whose `POST` is still in flight; the boundary fires; block B's only partial is `"Reverting"`, a prefix of block A's `"Reverting the bad commit and watching CI"`, and arrives during the boundary await.

```
===== monitor onAssistantMessageStart ordering = OLD (await, then reset) =====
   post-1 message="Reverting the bad commit and watching CI"
   distinct posts: 1
   => block B was DROPPED: its prefix partial was deduped against stale block-A text during the boundary await.

===== monitor onAssistantMessageStart ordering = NEW (start split, reset synchronously, then await) =====
   post-1 message="Reverting the bad commit and watching CI"
   post-2 message="Reverting"
   distinct posts: 2
   => block B preserved on its own post.
```

A committed regression for this lives at the monitor closure level, which is only reachable by driving `subscribeEmbeddedAgentSession` (core `src/agents`) together with the real stream; importing core internals from an extension test would break the plugin boundary (`extensions/AGENTS.md`), so this is proven via the embedded-path capture above rather than a colocated unit test.

## Real behavior proof (feature-level: block rotation)

This earlier capture demonstrates the core block-rotation feature (preview-disabled vs `streaming.mode: "block"`) and remains valid; the embedded/fire-and-forget callback race is covered by the two sections immediately above, which were captured on the current head.

Behavior addressed: Mattermost draft preview overwrites earlier text blocks within a single turn, and `streaming: "off" + blockStreaming: true` does not produce separate posts (#87322). User-visible symptom is message-loss across tool-heavy turns.

Real environment tested: Node 26.0.0 on macOS 26.0 (Darwin 25.3.0), local Mattermost-API-shape loopback HTTP server bound to `127.0.0.1:38765` with an artificial 120ms `POST /api/v4/posts` response delay to simulate live Mattermost server latency. Exercised the production `createMattermostClient` (`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/client.ts:93`) - including its `fetchWithSsrFGuard` adapter with `allowPrivateNetwork: true` - driving the production `createMattermostDraftStream` (`draft-stream.ts:56`) and the new `createMattermostDraftPreviewBoundaryController`. The loopback server speaks the live Mattermost v4 API surface: `POST /api/v4/posts` returns a `{id, create_at, message}` body for the create path after the 120ms hold; `PUT /api/v4/posts/{postId}` returns the patched post for the edit path; `DELETE /api/v4/posts/{postId}` returns `{status: "OK"}`. Bot token, channel id, and thread root id are real-shape values. The AFTER pass deliberately fires the next boundary while the previous block's `POST` response is still in flight (`fastBoundary: true`) so the run exercises the race ClawSweeper flagged. The fix branch is at commit 353f83b794.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
git checkout fix/87322-mattermost-block-preview-boundaries
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
node --import tsx proof-87322.mjs
```

The script (`proof-87322.mjs`, not committed) starts the loopback server, imports the production source modules (no test mocks), drives the same callback sequence the inbound dispatcher fires for a tool-heavy turn - `onPartialReply` text block, `onToolStart` boundary, `onAssistantMessageStart` boundary, repeated - first with the boundary controller `enabled: false` (current shipped behavior), then with `enabled: true` (the new `streaming.mode: "block"` wiring), reusing the same client + channel + thread on both passes.

Evidence after fix: copied live console output from the loopback server with the 120ms POST delay and the fast-boundary scenario, showing the actual HTTP method, path, message body, assigned post id, and the controller awaiting the in-flight create before forcing a new message - 
```

[23:57:49.164]   controller → forceNewMessage() (awaiting pending flush)
[23:57:49.166] MM SERVER  ← POST /api/v4/posts  channel_id=C-channel-1 (held 120ms) → post-4 message="I found the bad commit. Reverting now."
[23:57:49.290]   controller → forceNewMessage() resolved
[23:57:49.290] AGENT      → onAssistantMessageStart  [BOUNDARY]
[23:57:49.290]   controller → forceNewMessage() (awaiting pending flush)
[23:57:49.292] MM SERVER  ← POST /api/v4/posts  channel_id=C-channel-1 (held 120ms) → post-5 message="🛠️ exec: `git revert abc1234`"
[23:57:49.415]   controller → forceNewMessage() resolved
[23:57:49.417] MM SERVER  ← POST /api/v4/posts  channel_id=C-channel-1 (held 120ms) → post-6 message="Done - revert is in. Watching CI."

===== SUMMARY =====
[23:57:49.540] BEFORE: 1 POST /posts (creates), 4 PUT /posts/{id}/patch (edits)
[23:57:49.540] AFTER : 5 POST /posts (creates), 0 PUT /posts/{id}/patch (edits)
[23:57:49.540] => AFTER produces 5 distinct Mattermost posts; BEFORE collapses to a single post with 4 in-place edits, which is the issue #87322 user-visible symptom.
```

Key timing detail in the AFTER pass: every boundary in the fast scenario fires _before_ the previous block's `POST` response comes back (e.g. `23:57:48.918` boundary fires while `post-2` is still being held by the server), and the controller's `forceNewMessage()` line shows it correctly awaiting the in-flight create - `awaiting pending flush` at t=48.918, then `resolved` at t=49.041, ~120ms later, exactly the server's hold time. The next block's `POST` only goes out after the resolved line. No `PUT` (in-place edit) is ever emitted, so the race ClawSweeper flagged at `draft-stream.ts:74-75` cannot collapse the next block onto the previous post id.

Observed result after fix: with the boundary controller wired in (the AFTER block above), the production `MattermostClient` issues `POST /api/v4/posts` for every text/tool block boundary - five distinct Mattermost posts (`post-2` through `post-6`), each carrying one block of the turn's content. The BEFORE block shows the shipped behavior on `main`: one `POST /api/v4/posts` for the first block (`post-1`), then four `PUT /api/v4/posts/post-1` calls that overwrite the visible message at every transition. Only the last `PUT` body (`"Done - revert is in. Watching CI."`) is what a Mattermost user actually sees - earlier text blocks and tool calls are gone. The patched path preserves them as their own posts. Same `MattermostClient` build, same channel, same thread, same callback sequence - only the controller's `enabled` flag differs. The terminal capture above is the exact stdout from the loopback HTTP server logging every inbound request as it lands.

Supplemental unit/integration coverage (not the primary proof; these only assert the same boundary the live capture shows above):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/draft-stream.test.ts` → 20/20 passed (includes the `forceNewMessage` regression, the `flushes a pending in-flight create before forcing a new post` delayed-transport regression, the `seals a pending partial onto the in-flight created post instead of duplicating it` regression, the `opens a fresh post for a partial that arrives before a fire-and-forget boundary settles` synchronous-detach regression, the new `splits the next boundary when a noteUpdate arrives while the prior boundary is pending` gate-clobber regression, and 5 controller cases).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts` → 10/10 passed (after extending the existing draft-stream module mock with a no-op controller stub; the `keeps consecutive tool-progress updates on one post in block streaming` case now drives distinct rendered progress lines).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/` → 29 files / 377/377 passed (full mattermost dir suite, includes `monitor.test.ts` and `accounts.test.ts`).
- `pnpm tsgo:core` / `pnpm tsgo:extensions` / `pnpm check:test-types` → all exit 0.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/` and `oxfmt --check` on touched files → exit 0.
- `pnpm check:bundled-channel-config-metadata` → exit 0 (canonical `streaming.mode` values already shipped; no schema change in this PR).

What was not tested: A self-hosted Mattermost 11.6.2 Team Edition Docker server with a real OpenClaw bot account and a real provider running an exec-heavy agent was not exercised end-to-end here - that environment was not reachable from this checkout. The capture above instead drives the same production `createMattermostClient` (including its SSRF-guarded fetch adapter) against a v4-API-shape loopback server on `127.0.0.1`, so the HTTP-level behavior the live Mattermost server would see is identical, but the Mattermost server-side rendering pipeline (notification fan-out, mobile push, etc.) was not observed. The reporter on #87322 can confirm the user-visible result against their Mattermost 11.6.2 server by following the same `streaming.mode: "block"` config on the fix branch.

## Refs

- Fixes #87322
- Related (not closed): #75256 - overlapping branch attempted a narrower `streaming.mode = "partial" | "block"` config that CLAWsweeper flagged as schema-narrowing. This PR keeps the canonical `streaming.mode` contract intact and only attaches per-mode behavior to the existing `"block"` value.
- Mirrors the Discord boundary pattern at `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.draft-preview.ts:132-138`.

cc the reporter on #87322 for the live Mattermost server-side verification path.

On `origin/main`, the Realtime Talk provider row truncates the provider setup text early, and related Voice setup/talk/dictation copy has little room for stable wrapping. ## Why This Change Was Made This keeps the visual cleanup scoped to the active Android Voice tab source. The change gives Voice controls predictable row sizing, allows provider/status copy to wrap where there is enough vertical space, and keeps compact controls ellipsized instead of forcing cramped boxes. The code change is limited to `VoiceScreen.kt`, plus the generated native i18n source inventory line metadata for the moved strings. ## User Impact Android users get a more readable Voice tab. Realtime Talk and Dictation setup rows have cleaner text boxes, the primary action row keeps its icon and label centered, and talk controls remain evenly sized. No Gateway API, authentication, permission, or voice provider behavior changes are included. ## Evidence - Base refreshed to current `origin/main` at `a905eb42acda7083bbfcd70a21780cd954f61070` before publish. - `pnpm native:i18n:check` passed. - `./gradlew :app:runKtlintCheckOverMainSourceSet --console=plain` passed. - `./gradlew :app:assemblePlayDebug --console=plain` passed. - Real behavior proof: Android lane-b emulator connected to a local OpenClaw Gateway; the before APK was built from `origin/main`, the after APK was built from this branch, and the Voice tab was opened online in both builds. - AI-assisted: yes, Codex.
